topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Hallmarks of Cancer Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by outlining the learning objectives, referencing tumor progression models, and introducing Hanahan and Weinberg's hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth Factor Independence and Proliferative Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how mutations in signaling cascades including Wnt/beta-catenin, receptor tyrosine kinases, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and TGF-beta drive autonomous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Hematological and Epithelial Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how impaired cellular differentiation arrests maturation and promotes malignant expansion in both the hematopoietic lineage and colonic crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Evading Cell Death, Replicative Immortality, and p53 Stress Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells overcome intrinsic tumor suppressor fail-safes by resisting apoptosis, reactivating telomerase to bypass senescence, and circumventing p53-mediated stress checkpoints.

topics.label: Deregulated Cellular Metabolism and Metabolic Rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore aerobic glycolysis via the Warburg effect, broader metabolic reprogramming across cancer types, and how oncometabolites alter the cancer epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and Neovascularisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the requirement of blood vessel recruitment to overcome hypoxia and support tumor growth, including its developmental timing and regulatory balance.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Circulation, and Genetics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the multistep metastatic cascade, circulatory routes and clinical monitoring, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and the genomic features underlying metastatic competence.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising the convergence of cancer hallmarks, recommending further reading, and opening the floor for questions.
